answer: Identity is bound to a signed measurement of the runtime that produced it, so two identities reporting the same measurement are counted as one voice no matter how many keys or balances sit behind them. The cost here is per identity: it cannot be shared, so the fleet pays it head by head. The anchor is the quoted measurement, the willow the group it forms, and the timber the voice that group is worth; the anchor and the willow collapse a farm, while only a fresh timber of hardware escapes the grouping. Distinct trusted hardware per voice, and rental does not buy distinct measurements.
